title: Epigenetic clocks and adverse childhood experiences: a meta-analysis
title_zh: 表观遗传时钟与童年不良经历：一项荟萃分析
abstract: Abstract Epigenetic clocks predict biological age from DNA methylation patterns, providing insight into cellular aging. Different clocks capture distinct aspects of aging, and their relevance to research areas may vary — including early-life stress (ELS) and adverse childhood experiences (ACEs). This meta-analysis evaluates which clocks are most associated to biological consequences of ELS and ACEs. A systematic search was conducted following PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO registration: CRD420251047805) to identify studies assessing associations between ACEs or ELS and epigenetic age acceleration (EAA). Eligible human studies used validated ACE or ELS measures and reported DNA methylation–based age from peripheral tissues. Data were extracted and pooled using inverse-variance random-effects models to generate beta coefficients and 95% confidence intervals (RevMan 5.4). Seventeen studies (n = 10,940) met inclusion criteria and used 8 epigenetic clocks: Horvath’s, Hannum’s, PhenoAge, GrimAge, DunedinPACE, DunedinPoAm, Skin & Blood and PedBE. Amongst these, GrimAge and DunedinPACE demonstrated the strongest, most consistent associations with total ACE counts and subdomains including abuse (total, physical, sexual), neglect (total), and household dysfunction (total, socioeconomic impact). Only DunedinPACE demonstrated robust associations across strata, with significant age differences and no sex effects. This meta-analysis highlights variability in how clocks capture the biological imprint of early adversity. Later-generation clocks like GrimAge and DunedinPACE, integrating physiological and mortality-related methylation signatures, show the most consistent with cumulative effects of ELS and ACEs. These findings emphasise the need for careful clock selection and rigorous study design in stress-biology research, with implications for identifying individuals at risk for EAA and stress-related disorders.
abstract_zh: 摘要 表观遗传时钟根据DNA甲基化模式预测生物学年龄，从而揭示细胞老化。不同的时钟捕捉老化的不同方面，它们对研究领域的相关性可能各不相同——包括早期生活压力（ELS）和童年不良经历（ACEs）。本荟萃分析评估了哪些时钟与ELS和ACE的生物学后果最相关。按照PRISMA指南进行系统检索（PROSPERO注册号：CRD420251047805），以确定评估ACE或ELS与表观遗传年龄加速（EAA）关联的研究。合格的人体研究采用了经过验证的ACE或ELS测量方法，并报告了外周组织中基于DNA甲基化的年龄。数据提取后采用逆方差随机效应模型进行合并，以生成β系数和95%置信区间（RevMan 5.4）。共17项研究（n = 10,940）符合纳入标准，采用了8种表观遗传时钟：Horvath时钟、Hannum时钟、PhenoAge、GrimAge、DunedinPACE、DunedinPoAm、皮肤与血液时钟以及PedBE。其中，GrimAge和DunedinPACE显示出与ACE总计数及包括虐待（总计数、身体虐待、性虐待）、忽视（总计数）以及家庭功能失调（总计数、社会经济影响）在内的多个子领域之间最强、最一致的关联。只有DunedinPACE在不同亚组间显示出稳健的关联，且伴有显著的年龄差异，无性别差异。本荟萃分析突显了不同表观遗传时钟捕捉早期逆境生物学印记的差异性。后代时钟（如GrimAge和DunedinPACE）整合了生理和与死亡率相关的甲基化特征，与ELS和ACE的累积效应具有最一致的关联。这些发现强调了在应激生物学研究中进行谨慎的时钟选择和严格的研究设计的必要性，对于识别表观遗传年龄加速和与应激相关的障碍风险人群具有重要意义。
